final_proof:
**Definition used.** A mapping $\psi: \struct{B_1,\preceq'_1} \to \struct{B_2,\preceq'_2}$ between complete lattices is a complete lattice homomorphism iff for every subset $S \subseteq B_1$:
$\psi(\sup S) = \sup \psi[S]$ and $\psi(\inf S) = \inf \psi[S]$.
(Suprema/infima exist since the lattices are complete.)

**Proof.**
*Step 1 ($\phi^{-1}$ is a bijection).* Since $\phi$ is a bijection it has a two-sided inverse $\phi^{-1}$ with $\phi^{-1}\circ\phi = I_{A_1}$ and $\phi\circ\phi^{-1} = I_{A_2}$. Hence $\phi^{-1}$ itself has the two-sided inverse $\phi$, so $\phi^{-1}$ is a bijection.

*Step 2 (images).* Let $T \subseteq A_2$ be arbitrary and put $S := \phi^{-1}[T] = \set{\phi^{-1}(t) : t \in T} \subseteq A_1$. Then
$\phi[S] = \set{\phi(\phi^{-1}(t)) : t \in T} = T.$
(Also $S \ne \O$ iff $T \ne \O$, so the argument is unchanged if the definition only quantifies over non-empty subsets.)

*Step 3 (suprema).* Since $\phi$ is a complete lattice homomorphism, $\phi(\sup S) = \sup \phi[S] = \sup T$. Applying $\phi^{-1}$ to both sides and using $\phi^{-1}\circ\phi = I_{A_1}$:
$\sup S = \phi^{-1}(\sup T)$, i.e. $\phi^{-1}(\sup T) = \sup \phi^{-1}[T]$.

*Step 4 (infima).* Identically, $\phi(\inf S) = \inf \phi[S] = \inf T$, so $\inf S = \phi^{-1}(\inf T)$, i.e. $\phi^{-1}(\inf T) = \inf \phi^{-1}[T]$.

Since $T \subseteq A_2$ was arbitrary, $\phi^{-1}: L_2 \to L_1$ preserves all suprema and infima, so it is a complete lattice homomorphism; by Step 1 it is bijective. $\blacksquare$
